scenes.heading: Retries & Dead-Letter Queues
scenes.narration: Retries recover from transient failures, and dead-letter queues catch the messages that will never succeed, so no data is silently lost.

scenes.heading: Transient vs poison failures
scenes.narration: A transient failure is a network blip or timeout that will succeed if you simply try again, so it deserves a retry. A poison message is fundamentally broken, perhaps malformed or violating a constraint, and it will fail on every single attempt. Distinguishing the two prevents you from retrying a doomed message forever.

scenes.heading: Why plain retries aren't enough
bullets: Retrying a poison message loops forever
Infinite retries block the whole queue
Backoff prevents hammering a struggling service
A dead-letter queue isolates the bad messages
scenes.narration: Retrying a poison message loops forever because it can never succeed. Worse, that endless retry can block every message behind it in the queue. Exponential backoff keeps retries from hammering a service that is already struggling, and a dead-letter queue isolates the truly bad messages so the pipeline keeps flowing.

scenes.heading: Retry with backoff, then dead-letter
scenes.narration: This handler retries transient errors with an exponential backoff that doubles each attempt but caps at sixty seconds. A recognized poison error goes straight to the dead-letter queue instead of wasting retries. And if the retries are exhausted, the message is treated as poison and dead-lettered rather than dropped, so nothing disappears silently.

scenes.heading: The failure funnel
scenes.narration: Each message is processed, and a transient error triggers retries with backoff. Once retries are exhausted, the message lands in the dead-letter queue rather than blocking the stream. An alert prompts you to inspect that queue, and after fixing the root cause you replay the messages so no data is permanently lost.

scenes.text: Retry with capped exponential backoff, cap the attempts, and always dead-letter the rest — a growing DLQ is a signal, not a dumping ground.
scenes.narration: Retry with capped exponential backoff, limit the attempts, and dead-letter whatever remains, remembering that a growing dead-letter queue is a signal to investigate, not a place to forget.
